en:
I see. Just like the Captain
said, this place is a strange
ruin. You want us to
investigate it, right?

I lack the Federation's
expertise, but if this is like the
Cursed Temple on Planet
Faykreed, I may be of some
use.

I don't really get it, so I'll leave
the investigation to you two. In
exchange, leave the enemies
on the way to me!
I'm counting on you, Erys. It\nfeels strange that you share a\nname with my daughter.
Oh, really? I guess we have a\nstrange connection then. It's\nnice to meet you, mister.
...Hey now, do I really look that\nold? Well, anyway, I'm counting\non you.

Hehe... This is our first time
working together as well. It is a
pleasure to meet you, Erys,
and Professor Bowman.
Yeah, nice to meet you. Let's\nsee...
It's Raffine, the Healer
It's Raffine, the Kronos\nresearcher
Uh... who was she again?

Ah, it's you! I've heard you've
been helping the Captain and
the others since the early days
when our numbers were still
small, right?
You're a researcher from\nKronos, right? You look quite\nintelligent.

Yeah... I've heard of you from
Faykreed. You're a Crest
Technology researcher
specializing in biology, right?

You've been a precious healer
since the crew was small,
right? So, you're a doctor who
also does research?

...To the Federation, we're just
a rival coalition on the frontier.
It's no wonder I'm forgotten.
...Um, my name is Raffine.

Oh, so you're Raffine! You've
been a precious healer since
the crew was small, right? The
Captain is terrible for
forgetting you.

Yeah... I've heard of you from
Faykreed. You're a Crest
Technology researcher
specializing in biology, right?

...It wasn't research to be
proud of, nor is it something I'd
hide now. That's why I am the
right person to study this
facility.

For some, facing the past and
its possibilities may be painful.
But I... we... had no other
choice.
Therefore... no matter what I\nsee, I will feel neither regret\nnor pain.

...Ah, I knew it. That was inside
the Kronos Central Crest
Research Institute. When they
came for Felria... Relia's other
half...
And you are?
I am Raffine. The... Biological\nResearch Sector Administrator\nof this institute.
Please, come with me. I will\nguide you to her.
Wait, why are you cooperating\nwith us?
Because... you are strong.
Strong?
Not every researcher in this\nsector is happy with the\nresearch we are conducting.
We don't want to involve any\nmore people in this project.
However, if we simply release\nyou from here, you will only be\nhunted forever.
We need someone who can\nprotect against both Kronos\nand the Federation.
This way, please.

I know this is forward of me,
but I beg you. Please free
those two from being mere
tools of war.

...We at Kronos feared the
immense power of the Galactic
Federation, which we first
encountered 16 years ago.

To weaponize our superior
Crest technology, we began
large-scale practical research
on Spacetime Crest organisms.

Many test subjects were
created, but only two were
able to successfully integrate.
They were the girls you know,
Relia and Felria.

You're so kind, Raffine. You
tried to save them, even if it
meant betraying your own
country, didn't you?

I am not kind... It was we
researchers who brought them
into this world as Spacetime
Crest Creatures.

...Being a scholar in service is
tough, being forced to do
things against your will. But it's
hard to chase ideals if it
means losing your livelihood.
Even so, the researchers\nworked together to ensure\nRelia could escape via shuttle.

We couldn't save Felria... in the
end, we failed her. Even what
you just saw was ultimately
discovered by the upper
management.

I am nothing like the heroes
who saved the universe... At
most, I can only save one
person... both then and now.
But even if it was only one... I\nam still glad that we were able\nto save Relia.

N-now that you mention it...
You betrayed your country,
right? What happened to you
all after that...?

You said you could only save
one... Y-you're just not counting
yourselves, right? Don't tell me,
even including you, it was only
one...?

Kronos was a harsh
organization. ...I wanted to do
something for my subordinates
who acted as those girls'
parents, but...

...This place is like heaven.
Unlike that final farewell, where
we even hesitated to embrace
one another... I doubt there will
be such sadness again.

I will do my very best to
protect the captain, who is the
heart of this ship, and the ship
itself. I will do everything in my
power, you know.

The exploration tips I got from
Ernest really came in handy.
There's a Gem under the dust.
Could you take a look, Raffine?

As I thought, this is from the
Temple of Cursed Sigils... I'll
cross-reference it with the
Quad Scanner I borrowed from
Coro.

After seeing that past, how
can those two just calmly
investigate and exchange
opinions? I expected more
conflict or hesitation...
Because they're adults
Because they're scholars
Because of Still Waters?
Do you have something on your\nmind?

...I see, 27 and 29. I guess
they've become completely
detached from that kind of
youthful conflict.
I wonder if the Captain is the\nsame way?
...Scholars are amazing. It's a\nkind of Talent, isn't it?

...I see, Still Waters. No silence,
no confusion, and in many
ways, they never turn to
poison...

N-no, I don't! I wasn't wondering
what I would do, and besides,
they're here knowing all of
this...
...I said, there's nothing! There's\nreally nothing!

...Hey, Professor Bowman.
Aren't you afraid? Of having
your past or your possibilities
seen by others?

As long as it's nothing I
wouldn't show a child, I guess
I'm not afraid. I've shared most
things with Claude and my wife
anyway.
...You're strong. Little Erys is\nso lucky to have such a strong\nfather.
I suppose. Though that doesn't\nmean... it doesn't hurt at all.
...I can see it. Is that Linga's\ntown...? No, it's the port town\nof Harley.

If so, this is when I was just
returning from fetching the
herb Metox for a girl suffering
from a serious illness...
Ma'am! How is your daughter's\ncondition?
Mother: Oh, it's terrible! This\nchild, she just suddenly\ncollapsed!
Mother: Please, I beg you. Save\nmy daughter... save Elanor!
Ugh!? She's fallen into a\ncoma...?
If I use the medicine made by\ncompounding this Metox, the\nillness should be cured.
However...
However, what is it?
That is, if this girl has enough\nstrength left in her...
What?!
Given the current situation, it's\nabout a fifty-fifty chance.

They say this Aiaro disease
progresses slowly, so even
without treatment, she could
likely live for another year.
One year...

But... if her weakened body
cannot withstand the potency
of the medicine, she might die
as soon as tomorrow.

Of course, if we don't
administer the medicine
immediately, her chances of
survival will only continue to
dwindle...

You must decide, Mother.
Whether to let your daughter
live a limited life of only one
year...
Or to take the risk and bet on\nher future...
Mother: Ah! No... I can't... I can't\nmake such a terrifying choice!
It's no wonder. Her own\ndaughter's life is on the line...
Claude, you decide.
What... But?!
I know what you're thinking.\nHowever...

A mother's heart cannot bear
the weight of the guilt, knowing
she let her daughter die by her
own choice.
She will need someone to shift\nthat responsibility onto.
I understand...
...Th-this is... so... cruel... Kuro...\nBut, but...

Erys, you don't have to force
yourself to say anything. There
is no right answer in a situation
like this.

I feel bad for forcing such a
heavy decision on Claude, who
isn't even a doctor, just
because he brought the
herbs...
But there was no one else\nsuitable... In the end, I wonder\nwhat Claude's answer was...
It's better to bet on the\npossibility
Give it our all for one year,\nperhaps

Ah, that's right, that's right.
Look... the scene from that
time is playing back in my
mind.
Rather than letting her live in\nagony, it would be better for\nthis girl to bet on a possibility.
I can't just let her die in vain\nlike this. Her life has only just\nbegun...
I feel the same way.
Is that alright with you too,\nma'am?
Mother: Yes... please, I'm\ncounting on you.
Alright! From here on, it's the\njob of a doctor―which is me!
Eh!? But...
A human life is a far heavier\nthing than you realize.
Far too heavy for you to carry\nall on your own...
Bowman...
Ah, that's right. Look... the\nscene from that time is being\nreplayed.
If she had one more year, I'm\nsure this girl could have left\nsomething behind in this world.
We can't take such a\ndangerous gamble. The odds\nare far too heavily against us.
It's unfortunate, but all we can\ndo now is have her live out her\nremaining year to the fullest.
I see... You might be right.
Is that alright with you, ma'am?
Mother: ...Yes...
Huh!? Mom...?
Mother: Ugh... Elanor...
What's wrong? Why are you\ncrying?
Bowman... We really are so\npowerless, aren't we...?

Well... after all these years in
this job, things like this happen.
You did well. Hold your head
high...

...She's safe, right? This child is
safe in the end? We went
through all the trouble of
gathering herbs; it would be
terrible if we failed!

Well, medicine has its limits no
matter how much effort you
put in. In the end, it often
comes down to luck.

Unless someone's around to
take that bad luck. Well, I'm
sure we'll see a different
conclusion one day.

...Life can be turned to ash so
easily... yet saving a life that's
fading away is so incredibly
difficult...

...It's no use hiding it from the
Captain now. But... I have a
past where I was brainwashed
and forced to be an assassin.

...That must have been
incredibly painful. Are you sure
it's okay for us to witness
those memories of your past...?

To be honest, I came here
thinking I should face it alone,
just to reaffirm the things I've
done...

Because without moments like
this, I might get swept up in
the Captain's cheer and forget
my sins.
But...

...Drowning in lonely
introspection isn't healthy. If it
means learning it together,
then I'll stick by you.
He's right. Please don't worry.\nWe could never hate you.
Thank you... Then... watch\nclosely. My... past!

I wonder which town that is?
Was it during the
assassination? Or the town
where they threw stones after
my memories returned...?
Woof! Woof woof woof!
...Eh? A dog is barking? I don't\nrecall there being a dog at the\nscene... Oh, is Lati there too?
Dog: Grrr, grrr...
Girl: Hey, stop barking! This\nperson isn't a bad person!
Y-yeah, that's right, he's not a\nbad person...
Dog: Grrr... Woof woof woof\nwoof!
Girl: Geez, I told you to stop!
...Lati, are you scared of the\ndog?
No, I actually like them... but\nwouldn't anyone be startled if\nthey were barked at?
Dogs are just judging whether\na person looks like they might\nharm their master.
Dog: Grrr...
See? I'm not an enemy~.
Dog: Grrr, grrr...
Do you want to be turned to\nash?
Dog: Yip... Yip yip yip!
See? I told you. You can\ncommunicate through vibes.
...Huh?
Erys...?

I-It was a mistake! That was
just some kind of mistake.
Come on, ruins! Play something
more appropriate!
Really? Gray is a lovely color.
...Watching wicked monsters\nturn to ash is quite refreshing.\n...Hehehehehe...
Hey, I heard you were going to\ndraw my portrait...
I see... So now you're just going\nto ignore me...?
...Hehe... Ahaha! What is this,\nsome kind of punishment\ngame?
Let's turn this ruin to ash. It's\ngray to begin with, so it'll fit\nright in.

C-Calm down, I won't hate you
for this. ...Though I do wish I'd
reconsidered my daughter's
name.

Exactly. One can tell that's just
how she is if you watch her for
a while. It's a bit late for that
now...!
Everyone, turn to ash!

This story has concluded. We
plan to release various other
stories in the future. Please
look forward to them.
